extracted.intended_audience: NBA fans, sports readers, and followers of trade-deadline reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and explanatory sports-news coverage focused on NBA trade-deadline rumors, completed deals, team strategies, and the factors teams weigh when making trades. Emphasizes sources, contract details, roster fit, and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade return priorities (picks vs young players)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams (e.g., Memphis) want picks or young players in return for stars; front offices often ask for 'picks or young players' when gauging the market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article examples: 'Memphis still wants picks or young players.' 'The Bucks...wanted a young blue-chip talent and or a surplus of draft picks.' Use whether offers are pick-heavy or player-centric to judge seriousness and fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Playing-style fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the incoming player mesh with the team's existing playing style (tempo, ball movement, usage)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example guidance: 'Would James Harden mesh with the Cleveland Cavaliers’ more up-tempo, ball-movement style? ... Harden holds the ball an average of six seconds per touch this season... Cleveland pushed for faster ball movement.' Evaluate on-ball usage, touches per possession, and whether the player's tendencies conflict with team identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract and salary-cap implications
rubrics_metrics.description: How a player's contract (guarantees, player options, remaining years, salary) affects trade feasibility and team planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article details: Harden's player option and guarantee split; Clippers preserving cap space for 2027; 'Harden has a player option for $42.3 million next season, however, just $13.3 million of that is guaranteed.' Use contract length, guarantees, and future cap targets to assess whether teams will make or avoid deals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injury history and current health
rubrics_metrics.description: Players' current injuries and medical histories factor into trade value and immediate roster impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Darius Garland's toe surgery and ankle sprain; Walker Kessler out injured; Anthony Davis hand injury. Use recent surgeries, lingering issues, and missed games to discount value or increase risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team strategy and timeline (rebuild vs contend vs tank)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding whether a team is rebuilding, retooling, contending, or tanking determines acceptable returns and targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrases: 'The Grizzlies are in full rebuild mode.' 'The Utah Jazz ... may be tanking this season.' Teams in rebuild mode seek picks/young players; contenders seek immediate upgrades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: deadline vs offseason
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a move happens at the trade deadline or in the offseason changes acceptable trade structure and leverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'may have a Morant trade before the deadline' vs expectation Bucks might wait until summer. Deadline trades often require urgency and different price expectations than offseason deals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Player willingness / input
rubrics_metrics.description: A player's preferences, public statements, and cooperation influence trade likelihood and destination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Giannis saying he has 'Zero' input; Harden denying he requested a trade; 'My sense with the Lakers is ... it only happens if Antetokounmpo puts his thumb on the scale.' Player-driven moves ('thumb on the scale') can precipitate or accelerate deals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market availability / scarcity
rubrics_metrics.description: How many players fitting a need are actually available on the market affects urgency and pricing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'The problem is that those guys are just not on the market.' If targets are scarce, teams may overpay or postpone moves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft-pick structure and protections
rubrics_metrics.description: The specifics of draft-pick compensation (protected picks, pick swaps, number of firsts) are central to deal valuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: '2030 protected Warriors first-round pick'; 'three first-round picks' in Jackson trade; top-eight protections. Protected picks, swaps, and multi-year packages materially change a deal's value.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBA and salary-matching rules
rubrics_metrics.description: League/CBA mechanics (salary matching, aprons, trade eligibility) determine what trades are legal or feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Harden and Garland can be traded for each other straight up under the CBA ... because Harden makes about $300,000 less than Garland.' Consider apron rules and second-apron exceptions when evaluating legality and complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positional fit and roster needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Trades are judged by how well the incoming player fills a positional gap (3&D wing, interior presence, point guard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Lakers have been in the market for a 3&D wing'; 'Celtics looking to upgrade ... front line.' Assess whether the player addresses a clear rotation need or creates redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future cap and long-term planning
rubrics_metrics.description: How a trade affects future cap flexibility, long-term contracts, and offseason plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Clippers preserving 2027 cap space; Mavericks resetting books; 'This also messes with their 2027 cap-space plan as Garland is under contract for that season.' Weigh short-term gain vs long-term flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing and credibility of reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability is judged by reporters, multiple independent confirmations, and named league sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites Shams Charania, Jake Fischer, Grant Liffman, Kelly Iko, etc. Language like 'reports' and 'multiple reports' and who breaks the story affect trust—multiple reputable sources increase credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemistry and rotation/defensive impact
rubrics_metrics.description: How a player's style affects team defense, rotations, and chemistry (e.g., ball-dominant players reducing team defense or ball movement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'How would the ball-dominant Harden and Donovan Mitchell mesh as a backcourt? ... this would not be good for the Cavaliers’ defense.' Consider defensive fit and how roles shift in lineups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of expiring contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Expiring deals are trade assets because they can be used to clear salary or be appealing for short-term pushes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Anfernee Simons is on an expiring $27.7 million contract, which means a deal for someone such as Nikola Vučević...' Expiring contracts often enable salary relief or one-year additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighing present competitiveness vs future assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams must decide whether to spend future picks/assets now to improve immediately or preserve them for later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Lakers willing to trade a 2031 first for the right deal but aware of future options; 'better options in the future that they could limit with the wrong move now.' Use opportunity cost analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market valuation changes after other trades/events
rubrics_metrics.description: A player's perceived price can drop or rise based on other blockbuster deals or market moves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'multiple reports that the price has dropped (but Memphis still wants picks or young players)' after Desmond Bane trade and the Jaren Jackson Jr. trade. Monitor how recent transactions shift market expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buyouts and post-deadline movement
rubrics_metrics.description: Players bought out after the deadline can join contenders and affect roster-building strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Khris Middleton will be bought out and could look to join a contender after the deadline.' Teams consider potential post-deadline signings when structuring deals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Luxury tax and repeater-tax consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners' tolerance for luxury-tax payments and repeater-tax exposure influences trade decisions and roster moves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Nuggets aiming to 'duck the luxury tax'; explanation of repeater tax as penalty over multi-year windows. Financial penalties can push teams toward money-saving trades even if on-court impact is minimal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference between pick-heavy and player-centric offers
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams vary in whether they prefer packages heavy in draft picks or in players; that preference shapes negotiations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example differentiation: 'The Warriors have made a pick-heavy offer. Minnesota is more of a player-centric offer.' Knowing a target team's preference helps predict which suitors are more competitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team negotiating posture and priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a team negotiates strictly for organizational return, is motivated to move a star, or handles talks differently from other teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Memphis is not working with Morant in the same manner as other stars... The Grizzlies are seeking the best deal strictly for the organization.' Also 'The Cavaliers...have been working together to find a trade that works for both sides.' Use reported posture to infer likely deal outcomes.
